context: docs/MASTERY_PLAN_2026-07-31.md, the gate to Phase F3/F4. Branch bridge/native-consolidation-2026-07-31. Live editor UE427PuerTSMCP, pipe UE427PuerTSMCP_UE427PuerTSMCP_81d778e7_skyshader5, level /Temp/Untitled_1. Every live call went through a freshly built mcp-server/dist over stdio with MCP_UNREAL_PROJECT_ROOT / MCP_PUERTS_TOKEN_PATH / MCP_PUERTS_PIPE, because the session's own MCP server process predates the new schema.
design_decisions: The registry is consulted, not copied. BuildBlueprintFromJSON keeps a local dispatch case for the eleven types where the builder wants control of the node's shape and calls FBPNodeRegistry::Find for everything else, passing the node's params as the factory's ConfigJson with snake_case keys translated in one table. UBlueprintMutatorLibrary::AddNode is left alone; only its factory table is shared.

GetSupportedNodeTypes builds its registry half by asking the registry whether a factory is actually registered. A factory that is renamed or removed takes its node type out of the MCP schema rather than leaving a type that builds nothing, and a name listed with no factory logs a drift warning. The MCP enum, the native validation and the dispatch therefore cannot diverge in the direction that matters.

Only fifteen of the registry's forty-odd factories are advertised. A node type is advertised when its config keys are written down in the schema; publishing a type a caller cannot configure would be worse than not publishing it. The delegate and input factories need project input settings or a delegate property to point at, and MacroInstance needs a macro library path that was not verified, so they stay unadvertised.

Math is a gated table of named operators rather than a free function call. Each entry maps to a UKismetMathLibrary or UKismetStringLibrary function checked against the 4.27 headers, and an unknown op is refused with the full list before the asset is touched. The same functions stay reachable through a raw CallFunction node, so the table is documentation and a guard, not a ceiling.

Variables converge like components: same name and same pin type is a no-op with the default reapplied; a different type is refused rather than retyped, because retyping drops every graph node that reads the variable. The comparison is category, subcategory object and container.

Defaults are checked against the JSON type instead of coerced from it. FJsonValue converts freely - the string "yes" answers true to TryGetBool - and a default that quietly becomes something the caller did not write is the failure this path exists to prevent. Found by probing after the first build; the lax version had already been shipped into one live run.

Struct defaults reject a key that names no field of the struct. FJsonObjectConverter drops unrecognised keys silently, so {"x":0,"y":0,"zz":400} meant (0,0,0) and reported success. This is limitation 7 closed for this path.

Variable type resolution, default conversion and the conflict rules live in UBlueprintGraphBuilderLibrary, not in MCPPuerTSBridgeBlueprint.cpp, because that module already depends on BlueprintGraph for FEdGraphPinType and UEdGraphSchema_K2. The native command runs the same entry point twice in validate-only mode - once with no Blueprint for type and default checks, once with the resolved Blueprint for conflict checks - so a rejected spec never creates an asset.

The door proves motion through the graph rather than through a runtime read, because the native allowlist blocks read_property during PIE (limitation 14). The panel calls its own SceneComponent.K2_GetComponentLocation, converts it with vector_to_string, appends it to the marker with append_string, and prints. Before and after are the same code path, so the two numbers are comparable.

walls: No Timeline node of any kind, in the registry or the builder. A smooth door has to be a Delay chain or a Tick with a counter variable. The door uses a single Delay because that is the honest minimum that proves motion; nothing here animates over time.
No widget and no audio authoring surface anywhere in the native catalog, so the Phase F3 sound and HUD halves stay out of reach. This is not a vocabulary problem; there is no tool.

ForLoop and ForEachLoop are macro instances. MacroInstance is registered in FBPNodeRegistry but is not advertised: its macro_bp/macro_name pair needs a verified engine macro library path, which was not established here.

A Blueprint variable's default is not parsed by FProperty::ImportText. Four structs go through FDefaultValueHelper or InitFromString instead, and the two halves disagree asymmetrically: ParseRotator falls back to FRotator::InitFromString so P= Y= R= works, while ParseVector has no fallback and rejects X=0.000 Y=0.000 Z=400.000 outright. Cost one build cycle. Limitation 16.

UScriptStruct::ExportText is a delta export. Called with Defaults == Value it emits () for any struct with no native ExportTextItem, so FVector looked fine and FRotator silently became all zeroes. Cost one build cycle. Limitation 17.

notes: The strongest evidence here is a negative one turned positive: the door logs its own coordinates, so 'the door opened' is a number in the log rather than a claim about a screenshot. Runtime property reads are blocked during PIE, and this is the pattern that works around that permanently.

Three of the four C++ cycles were spent on silent-success bugs in engine text marshaling, all found by probes written to be rejected. None of them would have shown up in the door, which worked on the first build.
